need: Read a gate on its interval (lower bound for a higher-is-better line) instead of the point estimate, in options_dominance and decision_sensitivity
why: The sole survivor clears the pass-rate gate by a tenth of a point; the decider needs to see what survives if the gate is read on the whole interval (nothing, on this snapshot) and whether the latency budget then decides
workaround: dot_interval of pass rate with computed intervals for the configurations near the line, plus a sentence; the 'nothing survives' reading is stated as an inference from two blocks, not a computed call

need: levers_effects and arms_compare on a percentile statistic (p95 latency), and settle_cases against a p95 budget
why: What retry and reasoning cost in tail latency, and how sure the pick's 87 ms clearance is, are both part of the call; levers_effects refuses latency_ms (no mean) and settle_cases says a p95 states no spread
workaround: range_bars of p50 to p95 per configuration against the budget, read by eye; the p95 clearance is carried as an open caveat with no size

need: Failure-mode counts per arm and task (the outcome measure) and kept_from for the example cards
why: To say where the pick's misses concentrate and which fix buys headroom; the outcome and extra_calls measures hold no statistics and examples_list returns an empty kept_from
workaround: Three example cards, one per task, stated as illustrations with no claim about how many failures they stand for; task pass rates carry the where

need: Case counts per task, so task pass rates carry intervals
why: The pick's multi-hop rate is its weakest task and the lead for a fix, but tasks state no count, so the block draws bare points and nothing says whether multi-hop is separated from the others
workaround: Task bars without intervals, called descriptive and uncorrected in the claim; no assumed_cases what-if, since no basis for a count exists

need: render_report: the whole page rendered from a draft report document
why: To reread the first screen as a reader and see how five claims, seven blocks and the explore controls sit together
workaround: Each block drawn alone with block_render and its values table read; the first screen reread from the JSON

need: A two-gate picture with intervals: gate_scatter whose points carry each axis's interval, or a dot_interval that reads two gated measures
why: The lead block shows the pick inside the shaded corner, but its pass-rate interval crosses the line, which only a second block shows
workaround: The lead gate_scatter, then a dot_interval of pass rate with computed intervals as its own claim
